observations.finding: The three families retain coherent subject identities across four complete fixed drawings each: helmeted charcoal Alliance Jenkins, green-grey fungal creeper and blue black/violet generic asari. No missing muzzle, boot, cranial ridge, claw or neighboring-frame fragment was observed in the actual native/scale previews.

All twelve held states were actually opened in four actual WorldView captures. The living aim/action/hit silhouettes remain complete, feet remain near the ground, and Jenkins tactical gesture, creeper reach and asari hand gesture are distinct. These declared held fixtures do not depict ordinary campaign progression.

The early Eden import displays Richard Jenkins in the three-member roster and as a complete standing combat body. The native Cover view shows his tactical gesture and separately rendered blue cover effect; the PNG itself does not supply that effect or a biotic skill.

The Feros native encounter shows two complete creeper silhouettes and the generic asari identity. The native shot/impact view preserves the encounter and target HUD. A foreground column partially hides the asari weapon/left arm and part of the body; this is retained as a scoped reserve in this first development phase.

Noveria field supports remain visible in exploration. Compared with the two frozen baseline views, the former central pillar no longer masks the three desktop rachni bodies in combat. Party bodies and the target list are readable in those reviewed desktop frames.

The390x844 Noveria view shows usable party/action/target panels and removes the former pillar obstruction, but the rightmost rachni reaches beyond the right viewport edge. Complete silhouettes on mobile are not certified.

Later Feros/Noveria imports show Ashley and no Jenkins in the party, but their preceding victories/recruitment were prepared with native Node functions. This development run does not play the first Eden victory, claim the loss scene or visually establish the full Jenkins-to-Ashley transition.
